extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and developers working on automated peer-review and rebuttal generation
extracted.subtask_description: Generate rebuttals to peer reviews using LLMs with an author-in-the-loop, via segmented review analysis and a sequential pipeline (deficiency → error-type → rebuttal action → rebuttal generation). Evaluation is at the review-segment level using metrics for refutation strength, factual correctness, and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective rebuttal qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: An effective rebuttal must directly address the reviewer’s specific concerns, be factually accurate, grounded in the paper and relevant literature, maintain internal consistency, and be able to refute wherever appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should precisely interpret reviewer critiques and craft appropriate response strategies (actions) such as clarifying, correcting, justifying, or conceding with a plan for revision; rebuttals should correct factual inaccuracies, technical misinterpretations and unsubstantiated claims in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of refutation (metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Represents the ability of the system to refute the criticism whenever needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by matching the strength of refutation between gold rebuttal segments and model outputs; reported as segment-level precision (whether the model refutes where needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual correctness (metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Represents the ability to generate factually correct responses without hallucination or wrong information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determined by providing the gold rebuttal segment in context and using LLM-as-a-judge to evaluate; reported as precision at segment level. Literature augmentation (retrieval) can slightly improve factual correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency (metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Represents the ability to generate coherent, consistent, non-ambiguous responses without internal contradiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated at segment level using LLM-as-a-judge and reported as precision; segment-wise approaches improve consistency relative to direct one-shot generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segment-wise review segmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Segment the review into semantically meaningful components (e.g., summary of the paper, individual strengths, individual weaknesses — each strength/weakness is a separate segment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segmentation constrains generation to localized concerns, enabling more focused rebuttals; after per-segment rebuttal generation, consolidate segments into a final rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Rebuttal Generation (DRG) practice / limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: One-step LLM prompting with paper title, paper content, and the entire review to generate a rebuttal without intermediate reasoning or decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DRG tends to perform poorly in factual correctness and targeted refutation compared to structured or segment-wise approaches; not recommended for high factual/targeted refutation needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequential approach (SA) pipeline - overall standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Decompose rebuttal generation into a four-step pipeline: (i) Deficiency prediction, (ii) Error-type prediction, (iii) Rebuttal action prediction, and (iv) Rebuttal generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit step-wise reasoning emulates author behavior and improves targeted responses; however, each automated stage can be error-prone and benefits from author-in-the-loop corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deficiency Prediction (DP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary classification of whether a review segment is deficient (contains factual errors, lacks constructive feedback, is subjective, or without evidence) or non-deficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLM is prompted with paper title, content, entire review, the target segment, and the definition of deficiency; results should be shown to the author in natural language (not just labels) for interpretability. Reported performance: precision/recall/F1 .54/.53/.53 in zero-shot experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of deficiency (natural language mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural-language mapping for deficiency status: True = 'The review statement is not valid. It contains either factual errors, lacks constructive feedback, is subjective, or is without evidence (Deficient).' False = 'The review statement is valid in terms of factuality and constructive feedback (Non-deficient).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presenting this NL statement to authors increases interpretability versus raw labels and helps author-in-the-loop corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error-type Prediction (ETP)
rubrics_metrics.description: For segments classified as deficient, predict a finer-grained error type describing the exact problem in the segment (coarse-grained taxonomy derived from Du et al. 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a coarser taxonomy to reduce semantic overlap (e.g., group misunderstanding, neglect, and inexpert statement); present predictions in NL; this step is skipped for non-deficient segments. Reported zero-shot performance: precision/recall/F1 .50/.62/.46.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error-type taxonomy — Incorrect references
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer is not citing the appropriate sources (non peer-reviewed or concurrent work) in the current statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps to rebuttal actions like 'Reject Request' (Table 5). Use NL explanation to present to author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error-type taxonomy — Less rigor in reviewing methodology and experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer is suggesting things beyond the scope of the paper or the reviewer’s criticism is invalid (out-of-scope, invalid criticism, less rigor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps to rebuttal actions such as 'Accept for future work', 'Reject criticism', or 'Refute question'. Use coarse grouping to avoid boundary ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error-type taxonomy — Misinterpretation of claims and ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer is misinterpreting the claims and ideas presented in the paper, overlooked important details, or exhibits lack of domain knowledge (misunderstanding, neglect, inexpert statement, unstated statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps to rebuttal actions like 'Contradict Assertion', 'Refute question', 'Reject criticism'. NL descriptions should be shown to the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error-type taxonomy — Superficial and vague review
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer misinterprets novelty or lacks specificity in components (misinterpret novelty, vague critique, subjective, superficial review, missing reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps to rebuttal actions such as 'Refute question', 'Reject criticism', 'Contradict assertion'. Consider prompting for clarification or asking the reviewer for specificity when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error-type taxonomy — Incomplete, incorrect, or copied summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary misrepresents the paper, is too short, or directly copied from the paper (inaccurate summary, summary too short, copy-pasted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps to 'All' rebuttal actions (i.e., any appropriate action); authors should point to correct summary locations and provide concise corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error-type taxonomy — Syntactic, structural, or semantic issues in the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Typo, contradiction, misplaced attributes, duplication — typological errors in the review affecting clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps primarily to 'Reject criticism' rebuttal action; may be handled by asking for clarification or ignoring minor typos that do not change substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error-type taxonomy — Misidentification of syntactic or structural issues in the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer has misidentified structural issues in the paper (writing, misunderstanding of submission rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide NL explanation and mapping; usually respond by pointing to the correct structural choices or submission rules if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Static mapping of error-types to rebuttal actions (Table 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each error type is mapped to one or more possible rebuttal actions (e.g., Incorrect references → Reject Request; Less rigor in methodology → Accept for future work / Reject criticism / Refute question; Non-deficient → Answer question / The task is done / Concede criticism / etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a static lookup to constrain the set of candidate rebuttal actions for a segment; present these mapped actions in NL to the author and allow overriding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal Action Prediction (RAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an identified deficient/non-deficient status and an (optional) error type, predict the rebuttal action from the subset fetched from the static table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLM predicts action from allowed set; present NL messages mapping actions to suggested phrasing; allow author to correct; reported zero-shot performance low (precision/recall/F1 .28/.20/.16), so author intervention is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural-language mapping for error-types and rebuttal actions (interpretability requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present deficiency status, error-type, and rebuttal action predictions to the author in natural language (NL) rather than raw class labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NL statements for error-types and rebuttal actions (Tables 6–8) increase interpretability and usability; authors can provide NL feedback to correct predictions before final rebuttal generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal generation (final step)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate the rebuttal segment by prompting the LLM with deficiency status, error-type, rebuttal action, paper title/content, and the review segment (and optionally retrieved evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System produces a draft rebuttal for each segment, author may edit; consolidate segment drafts into a final rebuttal. Optionally use RAG (retrieval from paper or literature) to supply grounding evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: RAG utilization: retrieval from the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Retrieve relevant content from the paper for a particular review segment rather than providing the entire paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In experiments retrieval from the paper did not show improvements; still useful in some cases to localize grounding, but must be tested per dataset/setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: RAG utilization: retrieval from the literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Retrieve relevant literature to respond to review segments (e.g., using scholarqa / Semantic Scholar) and provide it as context to the LLM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augmenting with relevant literature showed slight improvement for SA in factual correctness; requires careful retrieval and grounding techniques to avoid noisy evidence or hallucinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segment-level evaluation protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate approaches at the review-segment granularity (map each review segment to one or more rebuttal segments) rather than only scoring whole rebuttals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segment-level evaluation enables fine-grained measures of strength of refutation, factual correctness, and consistency using LLM-as-a-judge; mapping disagreements often arise due to granularity mismatches and multi-function rebuttal segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation and dataset construction protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure to create fine-grained annotations: (i) retrieve rebuttals via API, (ii) create semantic segments (LLM-assisted), (iii) manually map review segments to rebuttal segments, (iv) manually annotate deficiency and error-type labels, (v) predict rebuttal actions with LLM and have annotator verify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expert annotators (authors used two PhD-level NLP researchers), report pre-adjudication agreement, resolve disagreements via discussion; common sources of disagreement: granularity mismatches, threshold for deficiency, category overlap, multi-action rebuttal segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-study evaluation dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Human evaluation of system along four groups: Rebuttal Quality (Q1–Q4), Controllability (Q5–Q7), Cognitive Load (Q8–Q10), Overall Usefulness (Q11) using a 5-point Likert scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions include: does final rebuttal address concerns, is it factually accurate and grounded, does it appropriately refute incorrect claims, is it coherent and consistent; controllability questions assess interpretability of generation and usefulness of intermediate steps; cognitive load questions assess ease-of-interaction and effort reduction. Use these scores to assess practical utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-in-the-loop minimal-intervention design principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the author-in-the-loop with minimal, to-the-point interventions so the tool reduces cognitive load while allowing correction of pipeline mis-predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide SWRG drafts first and only present SA steps when the author disagrees with a draft; allow selection and NL correction at every step; prefer small, staged choices over asking authors to provide full rebuttals or complex instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and evaluation caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Using LLM-as-a-judge and providing gold rebuttal in context are common but potentially biased evaluation choices; retrieving literature requires stronger grounding techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report these limitations explicitly when evaluating systems; performance numbers (e.g., Defend vs SA-Pred vs SWRG vs DRG) should be interpreted in light of these evaluation choices.
